all_found.desc: [BUG] The TestFSMRootsAreDeclared tripwire only matches the quoted component `".metareview"` or `"docs", "metareview"`, so slash-joined literals such as `".metareview/runs.jsonl"` are never checked. That hides one FSM call site that still uses the wrong root. At internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:139, runsIgnored runs `git check-ignore .metareview/runs.jsonl` in workDir (the work root), and init calls it at run.go:333, but the terminal runs.jsonl row is written under the store root. If init runs from a linked worktree, or with a --work-dir other than the main checkout, the WARN_RUNS_NOT_IGNORED check tests ignore status in a checkout that never receives runs.jsonl. If the main checkout does not ignore the file, it can be committed there with no warning, and a spurious warning can appear in the other direction.

[ADVISORY] TestFSMRootsAreDeclared's doc comment says it covers every line in internal/fsm that builds a .metareview or docs/metareview path, but it misses slash-joined forms. Three sites have no root declaration and pass silently: wiring.go:139 (check-ignore .metareview/runs.jsonl in workDir), run.go:334 (the matching warning text) and record.go:89 (FSMRunDir: ".metareview/runs/" + ...). The per-site guard is weaker than it claims. A site written as a single slash-joined literal escapes it, so a store/work confusion can come back unnoticed, which is what #172 set out to prevent. Matching `".metareview/` and `"docs/metareview` prefixes and declaring or fixing the three sites would close it.

[ADVISORY] The new comment says TestFSMRootsAreDeclared enforces that every .metareview/docs path built in internal/fsm names its root, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md says every .metareview/docs path names which root it means. That is not true: slash-joined literals are never checked, and at least three such sites have no declaration. Readers trust that every root-sensitive path in internal/fsm is declared and checked, while an undeclared slash-form site (runsIgnored checking the work root while the row lives in the store root) stays unchecked.

[ADVISORY] The default export destination is still worked out in two places. The CLI rebuilds it itself (the workRoot/storeRoot fallback, then filepath.Join(work, "docs","metareview","fsm", id)) to report `out`, while export.Export builds its own from deps.defaultOutRoot(). Only the comment 'must match export's default' ties them together; export returns no resolved Out and has no DefaultOut helper. If someone later changes one default rule (the fallback, the path layout, or the root choice) and not the other, the CLI will report an `out` that differs from where the bundle was actually written, with no compile-time signal.

[ADVISORY] AC-1.5 in #172 asks for the two roots to be described in both §4 (The FSM) and §6 (State, evidence & storage). The diff adds the description only to §6 and a §10 gotcha; §4 still says nothing about roots or worktrees. One stated acceptance criterion is only partly met. Someone reading §4 to learn how FSM runs and exports are laid out will not find the store/work split there.

fix@0.summary: runsIgnored now checks the store root (TestRunsIgnoredChecksTheStoreRoot fails pre-fix: warned about the linked worktree). The tripwire now matches slash-joined literals via buildsRootedPath (TestFSMRootsAreDeclared fails pre-fix on record.go:89) and that site is declared. The comment and ARCHITECTURE.md now describe it as a tripwire, not proof.

fix@1.summary: export.DefaultOut is the single definition of the default bundle path, used by Export and reported by the CLI (pinned: reverting the CLI to build it from the store root fails TestLinkedWorktreeStoreAndWorkRoots). ARCHITECTURE.md §4 now describes the two roots.
